newsitem.title: USA: Iomega plans slim Zip drive for notebooks.
newsitem.headline: Iomega plans slim Zip drive for notebooks.

text.p: Iomega Corp said it plans to develop a slimmer version of its internal Zip data storage drive for use in notebook computers.

The company said the new design will be 12.7 millimeters thick, allowing it to fit in most laptop computers, making the Zip, with its capacity to store 100 megabytes of data a vialble replacement for current 1.44 megabyte "floppy drives."
A megabyte represents roughly a million bytes of data.
Iomega already offers a 15 millimeter Zip drive for use in the expansion slot of laptop computers. The 12.7 millimeter thick Zip will be a fixed, internal component in the laptop.
It said the 12.7 millimeter Zip is expected to be available to laptop computer makers for use in their machines by the second half of 1997.

The company said it has partnerships with VST Technologies and CNF Technologies to provide its 15 millimeter drives for use in Apple Computer Inc PowerBook computers and Compaq Computer Corp 5000 series laptops to be available in the first quarter of 1997.
